implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Handles the GET request for viewing a single event. Sets @event and @users for the view, enabling display of event details and assigned users.
implementation.name: show
implementation.pseudo_code:
On GET /events/:id:
  - Find event by id and assign to @event
  - Fetch all users and assign to @users
  - Render show view

missing_implementations: Remove button does not display a custom success message after deletion; uses generic notice.
No explicit error message handling for failed event deletion (e.g., if destroy fails).
No explicit check to prevent modification of user data from the event detail view (relies on UI, not backend enforcement).

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Provides a navigation link to access the event creation form, fulfilling the requirement for a 'New Event' entry point.
implementation.name: New Event navigation link
implementation.pseudo_code:
IF user is on any page
  SHOW 'New Event' link in navigation
  ON click, redirect to /events/new

missing_implementations: Success message must appear at the top of the main content area in green (currently uses Rails notice, but explicit color handling may be missing if not styled in CSS).
Error or alert messages must appear in red when something goes wrong (currently uses Rails alert, but explicit color handling may be missing if not styled in CSS).

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Fetches the list of users from the external JSONPlaceholder API. Only 'name' and 'email' are used for display and search. However, the implementation currently caches the user list for 5 minutes, which violates the requirement to load fresh data each time the assignment UI is opened.
implementation.name: JsonplaceholderService.fetch_users
implementation.pseudo_code:
Call GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users
IF response is 200
    Parse JSON and return array of users
ELSE
    Return empty array
Log errors if any occur

missing_implementations: The user list must not be cached locally beyond the current session (currently cached for 5 minutes)
No explicit prevention of user assignment from sources other than the external API (relies on UI and controller logic)
No explicit check that only 'name' and 'email' are used for display/search (other fields fetched but not used)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Provides a 'Remove' button for each event in the event list. The button triggers a confirmation prompt with the exact text 'Are you sure?' and submits a DELETE request to remove the event.
implementation.name: Remove button in event list
implementation.pseudo_code:
For each event in the list:
  Display event details
  Display 'Remove' button
    On click:
      Show confirmation prompt 'Are you sure?'
      If confirmed:
        Submit DELETE request for event
      If cancelled:
        Do nothing

missing_implementations: The backend does not call the external API DELETE /events/{id} (simulated per JSONPlaceholder API); it only deletes from the local database.
The success message after deletion is 'Event was successfully removed.' instead of the required 'Event was successfully deleted.'
No explicit green color for the success message text; it uses a green background but not guaranteed to match the non-functional requirement for text color.
No test or handling for simulated response from JSONPlaceholder API as described in the api_specification.

  ROUTE to corresponding EventsController action (index, show, new, create, edit, update, destroy)

implementation.How_is_it_connected_to_implementation: Handles event listing by fetching all events and rendering the index view.
implementation.name: EventsController#index
implementation.pseudo_code:
SET @events = Event.all ordered by created_at DESC
RENDER index view
